description: Primary-source material for issue #11 (development/testing effort). Internal R&D data — how many prototypes, how many failed iterations, how long a specific team took — is not disclosed by any manufacturer in the corpus and could not be found sourced anywhere. What is public and checkable is the other half of the question: what a product is legally required to prove about its own stability before it can ship, and how long that proof takes to produce. This file is deliberately thin — the ISSUES.md entry that opened this page calls it color, not a pillar, precisely because the interesting number (iteration count) is not obtainable and should not be estimated.
retrieval_notes: EUR-Lex refuses scripted access from this network (empty HTTP 202), same as data/regulatory.json. The 2013/674/EU guidelines text below was read from the legislation.gov.uk mirror of the instrument, which serves the same point-in-time text as adopted — this decision has not been amended since 2013.

eCFR was reachable this time (govinfo was used for data/regulatory.json's CFR text; the earlier note about eCFR bot-blocking a scripted client did not reproduce here for this section, so eCFR is cited directly).

One trade-press figure is included — a Cosmetics & Toiletries reader poll — and is labeled as exactly that: a self-selected 1-click poll of trade-magazine readers, not a survey with a disclosed methodology. It is the only concept-to-launch timeline figure found with an attributable, checkable publisher and date; broader claims about typical iteration counts turned up only unsourced marketing copy and were left out rather than repeated.

us_otc_stability.title: Stability testing
us_otc_stability.applies_because: Every product in this corpus carries an SPF claim, which makes it an OTC drug in the US — so this cGMP requirement, not general cosmetics practice, is what actually binds these twelve products.
requirements: a written stability-testing program with sample sizes and test intervals set on statistical criteria
testing in the same container-closure system the product is actually marketed in
an adequate number of batches tested to support the expiration date
accelerated studies may support a tentative expiration date only while full shelf-life studies are still being conducted — the tentative date must later be verified by real-time data or revised

source.type: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 21 Part 211 Subpart I
source.publisher: eCFR (Office of the Federal Register / GPO)
source.note: Text as displayed 2026-08-19, current to amendments through 46 FR 56412 (17 Nov 1981); unchanged since.

eu_stability_guidance.title: Guidelines on Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — stability of the cosmetic product
eu_stability_guidance.quote: The SCCS has recommended that 'relevant stability tests, adapted to the type of cosmetic product and its intended use, should be carried out.'
requirements: the safety report must show the tested composition matches what is actually placed on the market
a preservative efficacy (challenge) test where applicable
a determined and justified minimum durability, and a period-after-opening (PAO) where applicable
physical stability tests run in the actual market packaging, not just an inert reference container

source.type: Commission Implementing Decision, consolidated guidance text
source.note: Adopted 25 November 2013, published in the Official Journal 26 November 2013; guidance on Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, unchanged since adoption.

concept_to_launch_poll.caveat: A self-selected 1-click reader poll, not a methodology-disclosed survey — treated here as color, matching what the site's own issue tracker called this page, not as a sourced statistic on the order of the corpus figures elsewhere on this site.

source.note: Poll results as published; no raw vote count or respondent count disclosed.
